subject: InferInterop: delta triage and A/B runbook
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@edgescale.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: InferInterop follow-up: today’s demo + proposed A/B runbook

Thanks again for the call today, Sarah — good discussion and the demo seemed to land on the latency story. Quick recap and an actionable runbook so we can close the delta vs CloudMega you showed: 

Key takeaways
- You saw ~1.3s p99 on CloudMega for our core 256-token prompt set; Redwood showed a tighter p95 but with occasional p99 spikes during microbursts.
- EdgeScale cares about tail stability (p99 under load), predictable tokens/sec for bursty document ingestion, and cost per token at 95th percentile.

Proposal: Short A/B runbook (we want an apples-to-apples comparison)
1) Test corpus & traffic
  - Use the shared corpus (doc set + chat prompts) you gave. We'll add a second synthetic microburst set (10k requests with short TTL).
2) Measurement windows
  - Warm cache run (KV cache primed) + cold run (cold start/resets). Record p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Config matrix
  - Batch sizes: 1, 4, auto-batching (Redwood default)
  - Quantization: fp16 vs int8 (if available on CloudMega)
  - Model variants: rwd-7b-std vs rwd-7b-optimized (we'll supply both)
4) Acceptance criteria
  - p99 difference < 15% under warm-cache production traffic OR tokens/sec within 10% while cost/unit better than CloudMega.

What we need from EdgeScale
- Access to the trial endpoints you used for the CloudMega numbers (DNS or IP + test creds)
- Confirmation of the exact measurement interval and whether CloudMega’s p99 includes queuing time (important).

Owners & timeline
- Redwood: Jordan will own running the test harness and collecting metrics; Marcus will validate kernel/config parity.
- EdgeScale: Sarah to share test creds and the CloudMega measurement note by EOD Wed.
- Target: start runs Thu 6/20, wrap and share preliminary readout Mon 6/24.

Attachments: interop-test-plan-v1.pdf (first pass runbook we discussed).

Ask: Please confirm the measurement definition CloudMega used (did they include request queue, or only in-host latency?) and whether you can share the CloudMega raw CSV. If convenient, I'll set a short 30-min sync Thu morning to walk through the run matrix.

Best,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah@edgescale.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InferInterop follow-up: today’s demo + proposed A/B runbook

Thanks — this looks good. A few notes from the ops side that will affect the matrix: 
- We should pin the instance type for both sides (same vCPU/GPU class) to avoid hardware skew. I recommend NVIDIA A10G equiv for the 7B probes.
- Redwood will run two harnesses: (A) steady-state 1k qps over 10 minutes and (B) microburst 10k requests in 60s with controlled concurrency.
- We'll capture p50/p95/p99 AND distribution of request queuing time (to separate queue delays vs infer time).

I'll attach the runbook fragment we use internally (redwood-runbook.md) — it includes the Prometheus/Grafana queries for tail latencies and tokens/sec.

One ask: Sarah — do you have a preferred metric for "tokens/sec" (server-side decoded tokens, or client-side counted tokens)? We need to align the definition so our harness reports the same unit.

I'll stand up the harness in our staging VPC and send a test endpoint tomorrow. Jordan

From: Sarah Kim <sarah@edgescale.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: InferInterop follow-up: today’s demo + proposed A/B runbook

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before we hand over creds: 
- CloudMega report: the 1.3s p99 they quoted includes queueing (their trial harness funnels through a single regional LB). I’ve attached their trial report excerpt (cloudmega-report.pdf).
- Tokens/sec: for our billing and capacity planning we use server-side decoded tokens/sec (i.e., the tokenizer output at the model host). Happy to align on that.
- Hardware: EdgeScale uses a mix; we can stand up an A10G-equivalent for parallel runs.

Availability: We can provide trial credentials and the raw CSV by EOD Wed 6/19. Also happy to do the 30-min sync Thu 6/20 at 10:00 PT if that works for the team.

Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform Partnerships, EdgeScale
sarah@edgescale.ai | +1 (617) 555-0123

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@edgescale.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: InferInterop follow-up: today’s demo + proposed A/B runbook

Perfect — thanks for confirming the queueing detail, Sarah. Quick consolidation and next steps: 

1) Measurement alignment (owner: Jordan)
  - We'll measure server-side decoded tokens/sec (as EdgeScale uses).
  - We'll report p50/p95/p99 with and without queue time separated; include a column for "model-only latency".
2) Test window (owner: Jordan)
  - Warm-cache runs Thu 6/20 10:30–11:30 PT (after our sync). Cold-run window Thu afternoon.
3) Artifacts to collect (owner: Marcus)
  - Raw CSVs, prometheus histograms, GPU utilization traces, and the decode token counts.
4) Acceptance & decision criteria (owner: Kimberly)
  - If Redwood meets p99 within 15% and tokens/sec within 10% while providing a lower cost per 1M tokens, recommend moving to a focused pilot.

Action items for EdgeScale (Sarah)
- Share trial endpoint + raw CSVs (EOD Wed 6/19).
- Join 30-min sync Thu 6/20 10:00 PT to walk through the run matrix.

I’ll put the meeting on the calendar and share the Drive folder with the run results and dashboards (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-interop-test-plan).

Thanks — team will be standing by to kick off once we have the creds.

Best,
Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
